# Rankfolio

> Rankfolio is an SEO and GEO (generative engine optimization) content agency for finance. It writes sourced, dated content for fintechs, investment platforms and real estate firms, built to be cited by ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini, Claude and Google AI Overviews.

Key facts:
- Focus: finance only (fintech, investing, asset management, real estate, PropTech).
- Languages: English and French, native level.
- Track record: 80+ client reviews on Fiverr, 14 published finance and real estate pieces.
- Method: map the 10 to 20 questions buyers ask AI, run a dated baseline on every engine, publish citable content, re-run the same questions monthly.
- Contact: hello@rankfolio.io. Free GEO audit requests: https://rankfolio.io/#audit

## Services

- **GEO Audit** (entry, Free · [PRICE for full audit]): We ask AI engines the questions your buyers ask, and show you who gets cited, which sources they trust, and where you are missing.
- **Content Sprint** (pilot, [PRICE] · fixed scope): Four long-form pieces built to close the gaps found in your audit: sourced, dated, structured to be extracted and quoted.
- **Monthly Retainer** (ongoing, [PRICE] / month): Fresh content every month, plus your buyer questions re-run on every engine with a dated report of what changed.

## Work samples

- [Apollo Global Management ($APO): navigating the alternative investment landscape](https://rankfolio.io/apollo-global-management): Apollo manages $512.8 billion and posted record fee-related earnings of $516 million in Q2 2024 (+16.7% year on year), even as its shares fell on missed expectations. Five-year EPS growth of 52% a year outpaced 26% annual share-price growth, and a P/E near 12 in August 2024 suggested the market was undervaluing the firm.
- [Meta Platforms: a powerhouse investment opportunity](https://rankfolio.io/meta-platforms): Meta reaches more than 3.2 billion people a day and grew Q2 2024 revenue 22% to $39.1 billion, with profit up 60% and an 81% gross margin. It generated $23.4 billion of free cash flow in the first half of 2024 while Reality Labs lost $4.5 billion in the quarter. At about 25 times forward earnings, against roughly 50 for Nvidia, the stock looked reasonably priced for expected EPS growth of 23% a year through 2026.
- [Netflix: a streaming giant that keeps evolving](https://rankfolio.io/netflix): Netflix had more than 247 million paid subscribers in 2024 and spent $17 billion on content in 2023. Q2 2024 revenue reached $9.55 billion, gross margin recovered to 43.8% and annual profit rose from $1.86 billion in 2019 to over $5.4 billion in 2023. Its ad tier could exceed 10% of revenue by 2027, but viewing per subscriber fell from 2.1 to 1.9 hours a day.
- [ASML, the quiet force behind the tech revolution](https://rankfolio.io/asml): ASML is the only maker of the EUV lithography machines needed for the most advanced chips, which gives it a near-monopoly that Nikon and Canon cannot match. It reported more than €21 billion in 2023 revenue with gross margins above 50%; 2024 was framed as a transition year ahead of a 2025 upturn, with High-NA EUV and US export restrictions on China as the key variables.
- [Estée Lauder ($EL): a beauty giant at a crossroads](https://rankfolio.io/estee-lauder): Estée Lauder shares fell 43% over a year while the S&P 500 gained 18%. Adjusted EPS dropped to $2.59 in 2024, down 64% from $7.24 in 2022, mostly because of weaker Chinese luxury demand and travel retail. The Profit Recovery and Growth plan targets $1.1 to $1.4 billion in added net profit, alongside an AI Innovation Lab with Microsoft.
- [Starbucks: a new chapter with Brian Niccol](https://rankfolio.io/starbucks): Starbucks shares jumped 24% when Brian Niccol, who led Chipotle’s turnaround, was named CEO in August 2024. He inherits falling traffic (visits down 6%), a 7% sales drop in China and EPS down 6%, with a four-part plan built on baristas, consistency, the in-store “third place” and storytelling. The stock trades at a P/E of about 26 and yields 2.31%.
- [Project NED: the role of financial engineering in rapid and sustainable growth](https://rankfolio.io/project-ned): Financial engineering is the structuring of capital to lower its cost, optimize valuation and limit dilution. This white paper, written for advisory firm Project NED, contrasts Quibi, which burned $1.75 billion before finding product-market fit, with Zoom, whose revenue rose 325.81% to $2.65 billion and then held steady, and sets out the pillars founders need from first round to exit.
- [RentWise: investor pitch deck for a Paris PropTech startup](https://rankfolio.io/rentwise): RentWise is a rental management app for individual landlords in the Paris region. The deck sizes the Île-de-France market at €778.1 million to €1.04 billion a year, a €311.2 million serviceable market and a €31.1 million obtainable share, with revenue from a 4.2% management fee on monthly rent.
- [A simple guide to investing in waterfront homes in Florida](https://rankfolio.io/florida-waterfront-homes): Florida waterfront homes typically command a 25% to 30% premium over similar inland properties, driven by limited supply and steady demand from residents and vacation renters. Buyers should weigh location (Palm Beach for luxury, Fort Lauderdale for boating, Tampa Bay and Marion County for value), seawall and flood risk, zoning rules on docks, and flood insurance costs.
- [The ripple effect: how shifts in interest rates impact the economy](https://rankfolio.io/interest-rates): Central bank rates act as a lever on the whole economy. Lower rates make borrowing cheaper, support spending, jobs and risk assets, and can push inflation up; higher rates do the opposite. After euro-area inflation passed 10% in 2022, the ECB raised rates from its negative level, with direct effects on mortgages, savings yields and retirement planning.
- [The free cash flow analysis: what FCF tells investors](https://rankfolio.io/free-cash-flow): Free cash flow is the cash a company has left after operating expenses and capital expenditures: operating cash flow minus capex. It shows whether a company can repay debt and pay dividends, and it is harder to flatter than net income. FCF margin (FCF divided by revenue) measures efficiency; for SaaS companies, 20% to 25% is considered healthy.
- [Return on equity: how to read ROE, with Apple vs. AT&T](https://rankfolio.io/return-on-equity): Return on equity is net income divided by shareholders’ equity: how much profit a company makes with its owners’ money. Above 10% is a common benchmark and the S&P 500 averaged about 21.7% in mid-2024. Apple’s ROE of about 160% reflects high margins and deliberate use of debt, while AT&T’s, around 10% or lower, reflects acquisition debt and a mature, low-margin market.
- [Revenue growth: how to tell sustainable growth from hype](https://rankfolio.io/revenue-growth): Revenue growth only matters if it is sustainable. Investors should check what drives it (market expansion, product innovation, pricing, customer acquisition and retention) and whether margins, cash flow and the balance sheet can support it. WeWork shows how fast growth can collapse; Microsoft shows how growth backed by innovation and strong margins holds up.
- [The required rate of return: CAPM, beta and multifactor models](https://rankfolio.io/required-rate-of-return): Under the CAPM, the required rate of return equals the risk-free rate plus beta times the market risk premium, because only non-diversifiable market risk is rewarded. With a 3.15% risk-free rate and a 6.25% premium, a stock with a beta of 1.31 requires 11.34%. CAPM is limited by unstable betas and harder diversification, which multifactor models such as APT and Fama–French try to address.
- [Time value of money and net present value (NPV)](https://rankfolio.io/time-value-of-money-npv): Money has a time value: a euro today is worth more than a euro later. Capitalization projects a value forward (Vn = V0 × (1 + r)^n), discounting brings it back (V0 = Vn ÷ (1 + r)^n), and NPV compares the sum of discounted cash flows with market value. Turning €100,000 into €1.8 million over 10 years is a 33.5% annual return, not 170%.
- [Options explained: calls, puts, risks and hedging strategies](https://rankfolio.io/options): An option gives its buyer the right, but not the obligation, to buy (call) or sell (put) an asset at a set strike price before expiration, in exchange for a premium. A buyer can lose at most the premium; a call writer’s potential loss is theoretically unlimited. Investors use options to speculate or to hedge, for example with protective puts or covered calls.
